reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the premise that Mn leads to magnetic frustration in the quinary alloy, but it does not provide any data or discussion linking this frustration to an increase in effective stacking fault energy, nor does it address the subsequent chain of premises about SFE modulation, twin suppression, or the effect of Mn removal on mechanical properties. The key mechanistic links are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Mn induces magnetic frustration in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi
Magnetic frustration raises the effective stacking fault energy (SFE)
Higher effective SFE suppresses deformation-induced nanotwinning and fcc-to-hcp transformation
Removing or reducing Mn lowers effective SFE and relaxes magnetic frustration
Lower effective SFE enhances twin nucleation and transformation-induced plasticity, improving work hardening and ductility
